quote_text:
The team showed the right mentality as  a group—the players who started and the  
players who came in—by going into the  fight, which was necessary here against  
a Hearts team that went all in for the  victory with an offensive playing style,  
a lot of attacking players, and good quality. The  team dug in and took the right moments during the  
game. It's a pity that two times there was a  small offside—I didn't see the images back,  
but I believe VAR is always right—so we almost  scored two more goals in an away game, which  
is good. The team showed the right mentality.  Was it always top quality on the ball like in  
our best games? Not today. But the mentality  was right, and that needs to be the basics.
The result is always more important. I  hear that from you guys every week. If  
the performance is good and we don't get  the results, it's about the results at the  
end—always. That stays in football for every  club. You cannot say that the performance was  
not good today if you score three goals away  at Hearts and could have scored more with the  
offside situations. There were moments in  the game where we could have made better  
decisions, for sure, both defensively and  offensively, but the mentality was spot on.
I don’t think there’s one team in the world that  is expected to win every game without having a  
good goalkeeper. We know we have one. He  was the player of the year last season,  
so I’m happy to see Jack in  the form he showed today.
Clinton Ibragimov had a great game. It’s a tough  environment for a young man to come here with the  
crowd, and he coped so well. I need to praise him  today, and I don’t do that so often or so quickly  
with young players, but he’s showing consistency  from the moment he stepped into the team—in his  
work rate in training, his concentration, and his  performances in games. You see him developing week  
after week. Every meeting we have with him,  with individual images, he is so focused on  
getting better and so hungry to improve. Those  are the kind of young players you're looking  
for because they develop fast. I've had a few  in the past who made really big steps forward  
in a short time. He’s doing that as well. Now  the key is to keep this focus, concentration,  
and hard work going, and then he will be a  really good signing at the end of the season.
Is he further ahead of schedule than we thought?  Yes, for sure. I need to be honest about that.  
Credit to the recruitment team that found  him. Of course, we always have the final say,  
and we discuss things about profiles before  deciding. With him, we saw the technical qualities  
and the speed, but he didn’t have the positioning  at that moment. He made a lot of mistakes in the  
beginning when playing with the second team. But  he’s learning really fast. Credit to my staff and  
also to the experienced players around him—the  center-backs who have been working with him  
every day in training and coaching him. He’s very  hungry to get all this information from Robin,  
John, Liam Balogun, or Tav to become better,  and you see the evolution can go really fast.  
But the most important thing in football is  consistency. He’s been doing it for two months,  
and now we want to see the confirmation  over the next few months as well.
He has a calm temperament, which helps. Sometimes  players can be too calm and not aggressive enough,  
but he’s finding a good balance at  the moment. His choice-making is good,  
and with his left foot, he  helps the team by providing  
easier solutions—compared to when we had  to put a right-footer there in the past.
I think it’s now six games in a row where  Hamza has scored. That’s a lesson in being  
careful not to build players up too early and not  getting too excited when they are young. But it’s  
not just about goals for strikers or attacking  players. Today, for example, he started as a  
striker and ended up playing behind the striker.  He’s doing his job, working hard for the team,  
and showing good qualities. His decision-making  is really good in some games, and in others,  
he has a little bit less overview. But in two or  three years, he will be much better by taking this  
experience. He’s also someone who is hungry  to improve every week, watching individual  
images to make better choices for the future.  If he keeps doing that, he will keep growing.
In terms of the squad, do I expect anyone back  fitness-wise ahead of next week’s game? Maybe  
for training, but it will be difficult for  the game. Tom took his first minutes today  
after being out since September or October.  He was important in his smartness and being  
available between the lines. I hope to recover  one or two more bodies in training. Danilo will  
start training with contact now, which is  an extra boost. Connor Barron is close to  
returning, and Dujon Sterling is also close to  training. But we need to see their physical level.
It’s been an emotional week with a lot  of noise outside. Am I hoping things can  
calm down so we can focus on our work? I am  always focused on the team. I understand the  
disappointment because I I don't think it's with anybody more than with me after 
this cup game going out in this cup I understand that but I know what 
everybody's doing in the club to make things better and to make Rangers better 
for the future and I'm focused fully in that so I'm going to continue putting 
all my focus on those things like you said that last week one of the toughest 
of your fear did you feel any extra pressure just going into today's 
game uh extra pressure no I I just want to win 
all the games so I put this pressure on myself and the people around me also 
to to get that mentality so yes I was I was devastated after that game 
that cup game and I want like I said in the press conference I wanted to kick 
the ball myself over the line that moment because that would have made a 
hell of a difference and with that result we would have been consistent in 
2025 in this series of games now it's not so it's it's starting a new series 
and then putting all the focus in that thanks everyone
title: Philippe Clement Post Match Interview | Hearts 1-3 Rangers
